title: Pasqal neutral-atom arrays
summary: Quantum processors that scale by trapping more atoms in laser arrays.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Pasqal builds neutral-atom processors using optical tweezers to arrange atoms in programmable arrays, an approach that has scaled past a thousand atoms in research settings. Neutral atoms are strong candidates for quantum simulation of materials and chemistry, where analogue operation can deliver value before universal error correction. System-level fidelity and uptime remain the constraints.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2024–2030
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Simulation may be the first commercially useful quantum workload, which favours architectures that scale atoms cheaply.

What Would Change The View

  • Logical-qubit demonstrations.
  • Paid system deployments.
  • Error rates in larger arrays.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
